newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends at four month high, RBI watches.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends at four month high, RBI watches.

text.p: The rupee closed at 35.79/80 against the dollar on Thursday, up from 35.80/81 opening, and at its strongest level for four months, as the central bank refrained from buying the dollar.
Dealers said there was a lack of dollar demand, and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), which has persistently bought to halt the rupee's appreciation in recent months, kept out of the market.

The rupee's rise was more evident in the forward dollar market. Forward dollar premiums opened low, reflecting a series of interest cuts by Indian and foreign banks prompted by Tuesday's monetary policy statement by the RBI, dealers said.
The six month annualised premium closed at 4.97 percent compared to the previous close of 5.75 percent, they said.
Some dealers said the RBI's refused to buy dollars because the extra rupees coming into the banking system was aggravating excessive liquidity in the system.
Other dealers, quoting a recent statement by the RBI governor, said the central bank was leaving the rupee to market forces.
"With RBI out of the market, everything depends on SBI's net demand," said a dealer, referring to dollar demand from State Bank of India, India's largest commercial bank.
"SBI was a passive buyer today," the dealer said.
